title: How Unit Usage Sets the Refund Share of a Cancelled Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit Plan
content:
# Refund Share and Unit Usage — Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit

When a Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit plan of the Kessler Care Prepaid Maintenance Plans is cancelled, its refund share depends on how the unit was used. The facts come from two places:
- the unit's repair-order check-ins in the Service Accounts and Repair Orders records;
- the plan's own redemption entries.

All spans end on the effective date, which is the request date.

**Defined readings.**
- **Last recorded visit reading:** the highest odometer on the plan's redemption entries, whether reinstated or not. Where the odometer at sale is higher, or the plan has no redemption entry, it is the odometer at sale.
- **Highest check-in odometer:** the highest odometer written at check-in on any repair order for the plan's unit.
- **Unused-visit share:** unused visits (loaded, less redeemed, plus reinstated) over visits included.
- **Unused-mile share:** the expiration odometer less the highest check-in odometer, never below 0, over the plan's term miles.
- **Unused-day share:** the calendar days from the effective date to the expiration date, over the calendar days from the sale date to the expiration date.

**Rule.**
| Condition, in order | Refund share |
|---|---|
| The unit has a repair-order check-in more than the plan's service interval (5000 miles on the Kessler Care Fleet 12-Visit) above the last recorded visit reading | The lesser of the unused-visit share and the unused-mile share |
| No such check-in, and the plan has no redemption entry (reinstated or not) dated fewer than 12 whole months before the effective date | The lesser of the unused-visit share and the unused-day share |
| Otherwise | The unused-visit share |

**Edge of the first row.** With a last recorded visit reading of 40,000 (hypothetical), a check-in at 45,001 is more than 5000 miles above it. A check-in at exactly 45,000 is not.

**Worked figures (hypothetical plan).** The plan has 12 visits included and 8 unused; a term of 60,000 miles with an expiration odometer of 90,000; and a sale-to-expiration span of 1,000 days, with 400 days left.
- The unused-visit share is 0.6667.
- First row: with a highest check-in of 72,000, the unused-mile share is 18,000 over 60,000, which is 0.30. The refund share is 0.30.
- Second row: the unused-day share is 400 over 1,000, which is 0.40. The refund share is 0.40.
- Third row: the refund share is 0.6667.
